paper.title: NavHarness: Adaptive Goals for Agentic Vision-Language Navigation
paper.central_claim: An agentic VLN harness that couples adaptive local goals with goal-specific completion verification (Goal, Verify, Visuomotor agents) keeps execution consistent with the route and, with verified-completion memory compression, limits context growth; with the same backbone it beats Codex CLI on R2R-CE/RxR-CE (GPT-6-Astra SR 79.0/82.5 vs 74.0/76.3) and reaches 83.3% SR / 1.51 m NE over 24 real-world trials.
paper.claim_scope_note: The zero-shot superiority over trained navigation foundation models is a cross-cohort comparison the authors themselves call context, not a matched ranking.

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: a frozen frontier backbone is split into a Goal agent (local goal + verification question), a Visuomotor agent (primitive batches), a Verify agent (VLM judgment of the question from the latest observation; routes continue/revise/advance/stop) and a Memory agent (summarizes completed segments at verified boundaries). Controlled comparison: Codex CLI vs NavHarness with the same backbone, episodes and observation/action interface on 100 R2R-CE (Open-Nav subset) and 100 RxR-CE episodes, plus a three-backbone R2R ablation; all comparisons improve by 4-6 SR points. Goal vs verification is not separated (authors say so). Several SRs reported on 100 episodes are non-integer (62.6, 76.3, 82.5), so the number of runs or the effective denominator is undisclosed; no CI. Token budgets are not matched (RxR Sol Off 4298k vs Codex 2028k tokens). Verifier accuracy is never audited; STOP is not gated by it; final success is computed by the benchmark evaluator. Real world: Go2 quadruped, 8 routes x 3 = 24 trials, 83.3% (20/24), but no success threshold, no per-route rates, baselines are 'supplied aggregates'; movement budget value not stated. Initial view: credible same-backbone bundle gain with careful token accounting; isolation, statistics and real-world criteria weak.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: EVIDENCE.md transfer: harness built and evaluated in simulation, then run zero-shot on a physical embodiment (Go2 quadruped) and real scenes not used in construction, with stated trial counts (8 routes x 3 = 24). Lower bound: success threshold and per-route rates are not reported and the real-robot prompt adds platform guidance; these limits are scored in E.measurement/E.holdout.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With backbone, episodes and observation/action interface fixed, NavHarness (no compression) raises SR over Codex CLI by 4-6 points in all five reported comparisons (three backbones on R2R-CE, two on RxR-CE), with undisclosed run counts and no CI and with up to 2.1x more tokens; verified-completion compression saves 4-57% tokens at a 1-2 point SR cost; 20/24 real trials reported successful under an unstated criterion.
not_supported_as_stated: separate effects of adaptive goals vs verification
real-world superiority over baselines given as supplied aggregates
assessment.not_claimed: No reproduction; all results are author reports.

G.reason: Two concrete bottlenecks (route drift from unchecked local progress; history growth vs lossy truncation) with nearest lineage (agentic VLN harnesses, progress monitors, navigation memory); baseline drift not diagnosed and the compression motivation admittedly not a navigation failure mechanism. Both seats agree.

M.reason: Goal + observable completion condition + separate verification + completion-bounded compression is reconstructible with distinguishable predictions (larger gains on long RxR; drops at boundaries); verifier reliability is the untested core assumption. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, Eq. 1-13, routing priorities, evidence ordering and information permissions are reconstructible and STOP/coverage limits are stated; but the movement/interaction budget values are placeholders, the archived-image selection policy is unspecified, prompts are 'edited for readability' and the real-robot briefing is only summarized. Anchor 4 requires the chain to be fully reconstructible; these gaps hold it at 3.

measurement.reason: Simulation success is computed by the benchmark evaluator, but the effective denominators/run counts are undisclosed (non-integer SRs on 100 episodes) and the real-world success criterion is undefined with baselines as supplied aggregates. Anchors v2: undefined success criterion -> <=2; criterion present with incomplete denominators -> 2. Verifier never audited.

causality.reason: Same backbone/episodes/interface vs Codex CLI with consistent direction over three backbones, and Off/Goal as a single toggle; but the Codex->NavHarness step is a bundle, goal vs verification not separated, and token budgets differ up to 2.1x, so more model calls is an unseparated alternative. Both seats agree.

holdout.reason: No training, but development/evaluation episode overlap and RxR subset selection are undisclosed, trained-model comparisons are cross-cohort, and the real-robot prompt is platform-adjusted; real routes are new scenes but with an undefined success criterion. Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Anchors v2 'trial counts without variance -> 1-2': real repeats exist (3 per route) but are only aggregated; for the central simulation comparisons the run count is undisclosed despite non-integer SRs, there is no CI or paired test for 4-6 point gaps at n=100, and failure breakdown is limited to OSR vs SR. The lower end (1) reflects the undisclosed simulation denominators.

cost.reason: Per-episode tokens across all agents including compression overhead, cache and failed episodes are reported per backbone/benchmark, with exclusions disclosed; wall-clock latency and USD missing and budgets not matched (disclosed via the token table). Both seats agree.

resolutions.reason: Sim-developed harness run zero-shot on an unused physical embodiment and unseen real scenes with stated trial counts (24) satisfies EVIDENCE.md transfer (sim-to-real with trial counts / unused embodiment). Sol's objections (no success threshold, no route-wise breakdown) are real but bear on measurement quality, which is deducted in E.measurement, not on the level definition. Recorded as lower bound.

son55_value.reason: 完整 HTML 全文含附录 A-F、算法与提示模板。

resolutions.reason: The central SR claim (Table 1, compression Off) rests on the goal/verify decomposition, so decompose_and_delegate is primary; sol correctly identified the memory partition as a distinct operation, kept as supporting. Neither seat alone had both roles right.

C25 under the primary (model's own verify-and-revise loop during construction is executed); null under heterogeneous_decomposition because C04's magnitude/sensitivity-stratified compression of a trained artifact is not the operation.

Anchor 4 needs a fully reconstructible operation chain; the movement/interaction budget values are placeholders, the image-selection policy is unspecified and prompts are edited summaries, so the chain is reconstructible in structure but not in its operative parameters.

Anchors v2 binding: real-world success criterion undefined -> <=2; additionally the simulation denominators are ambiguous (non-integer SRs on 100 episodes). son55's own reason lists the undefined real criterion but did not apply the v2 ceiling.
